content.trans: 您想开哪种账户？

content.text: A checking or a saving account?

content.text: What features do they offer?

content.text: Well, if you just take a look here, see,

content.text: without checking account, you can have unlimited daily transactions for a small monthly fee.

content.text: And our savings account has a higher interest rate.
content.trans: 我们的储蓄账户的利息更高。

content.text: But you must carry a minimum balance of $10,000.
content.trans: 但是，您必须保持最低余额为人民币10,000元。

content.text: I see.
content.trans: 我看到。

content.text: Well, I think I'm more interested in a checking account.
content.trans: 嗯，我觉得我更喜欢一个储蓄账户。

content.text: I'd like to have easy access to my money.
content.trans: 我想能方便地访问我的钱。

content.text: All right, then.
content.trans: 好的，那么。

content.text: With this checking account, you'll be issued a debit card and a checkbook.
content.trans: 这个账户可以让你获得一个借记卡和一本存折。

content.text: Will you require overdrive protection?

content.text: There is an extra fee for that.

content.text: No, that won't be necessary.
content.trans: 对不起，我不太明白您的意思。如果您有其他问题或需要帮助，请随时告诉我！

content.text: In that case, I'll get you to fill out this paperwork.
content.trans: 在这种情况下，我会帮你填写这份表格。

content.text: I'll need your social insurance number and two pieces of government ID.
content.trans: 我需要你的社会保障卡号和两张政府身份证。

content.text: If you could just sign here and here, and here, we'll be all set.
content.trans: 如果你能在这里签名，这里，这里，我们就能搞定。

content.text: Would you like to make a deposit today?
content.trans: 是的，您想今天存款吗？

content.text: Yes, I'd like to deposit one billion dollars.
content.trans: 是的，我想把一亿美金存入银行。

content.text: One billion dollars.
content.trans: 一亿美元。

content.text: Oh, my God.
content.trans: 哦，我的上帝。

content.text: Okay, so an interesting thing here, not many countries use checks.
content.trans: 好的，这里有一个有趣的点：不少国家不使用支票。

content.text: That's right.
content.trans: 对的。

content.text: Right? The checkbook or a check?
content.trans: 是的，账单或支票？

content.text: Yeah, it tends to be more of an American thing, don't you think?
content.trans: 是的，它更倾向于美国式的东西，对吗？

content.text: It is. It is. I think it is.
content.trans: 是。是。我认为是。

content.text: For those of you who aren't sure what a check is,
content.trans: 对于那些不清楚什么是支票的人来说，以下是一些翻译：

content.text: it's basically a piece of paper that you just sign your name and...
content.trans: 基本就是一张纸，你只需要签名你的名字...

content.text: Yeah, you write the amount of money and then you sign your name, right?
content.trans: 是的，你写出了钱的数量，并且你签名了名字。

content.text: Right, and then you give that to the person that that person can take it to the bank and get
content.trans: 是的，然后你把那件东西交给那个那个人，让他去银行取款。

content.text: money in exchange for it.
content.trans: 钱换它。

content.text: Yes. It's not very common in other countries.
content.trans: 是的。在其他国家并不常见。

content.text: No, but from what I know, every single American has a checkbook and uses it.
content.trans: 是的，但我知道，从我所知道的情况来看，每个美国人都有一个银行账户，并且都使用它。

content.text: Right.

content.text: Yeah, yeah.

content.text: For example, you pay your phone bill or your electric bill.
content.trans: 例如，您支付您的电话账单或电费。

content.text: You just put a check in the mailbox and it's done.
content.trans: 您刚刚在信封上打了一个检查，这已经完成了。

content.text: It's an interesting thing.
content.trans: 这是一个有趣的事情。

content.text: Also, sometimes in other countries, people's salaries are paid through checks.
content.trans: 另外，有时在其他国家，工资通过支票支付。

content.text: Yes.

content.text: Oh, yes.

content.text: Pay check.

content.trans: 但是，例如，在中国，这并不常见。

content.text: Me neither.

content.text: What about in your countries?
content.trans: 在您的国家里怎么样？

content.text: We'd like to know how the banking system works.

content.text: Yes, come to our website at englishpod.com and tell us all about it.
content.trans: 是的，请访问我们的网站，告诉我一切。

content.text: Yes, and you can also leave your questions and comments on our website and we'll be there to answer it.
content.trans: 是的，您也可以在我们的网站上留言和提出问题，我们会在这里为您解答。

content.text: Yeah, Marco and I love answering your questions, so please visit us.

content.text: Right.

content.text: But until then, it's goodbye.
